items.headline: Sensex up over 1,200 points near 82,350 by midday and Nifty above 25,300 as banks lead after the holiday
items.summary: The bank index rose about 2.3%, with autos and financials strong; IT and pharma pared gains. Follows Monday's 81,106.65 close and Tuesday's holiday. Rally resuming; intraday figures.
items.rationale: Brent below $92, a firmer rupee and continued foreign buying lift rate-sensitive and oil-consuming sectors; higher US yields are a counterweight.

items.headline: Brent settles 1.17% lower at $91.49 after dipping below $90 for the first time since August
items.summary: It touched $89.16 as the US president said further strikes were unnecessary, then rebounded 1.1% to $92.53 on Wednesday after an Iranian official said no talks were under way. Down from $117.64 on 30 October. Easing, with a bounce.
items.rationale: Oil near $90 sharply lowers India's import bill, fuel-subsidy burden and inflation risk; the rebound shows relief depends on Hormuz.

items.headline: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October, above forecasts; 10-year Treasury yield back near 5%
items.summary: Core prices rose 0.3% for a third month. The 10-year yield jumped 13 bps to 4.992% and the 2-year 18 bps; a Fed governor said a half-point December hike is possible. Escalating rate risk.
items.rationale: Higher US yields and a likely Fed hike strengthen the dollar and can pull foreign money from Indian bonds and equities, pressuring the rupee and G-Secs.

items.headline: Rupee opens 19 paise higher at 93.74 per dollar on softer crude and foreign inflows
items.summary: Up from Monday's 93.93 close; markets were shut on Tuesday. Dealers see a 93.25–94.25 range, with rising US yields limiting gains. Extending gains.
items.rationale: A firmer rupee lowers imported inflation and oil costs; exporters' rupee earnings dip slightly.

items.headline: Foreign investors have put over ₹53,000 crore into Indian equities so far in November
items.summary: Up from ₹38,971 crore in the first week, after October's ₹52,100 crore exit. Strong second-quarter results add support. Ongoing reversal.
items.rationale: Month-to-date inflows now offset October's outflow, supporting large caps and the rupee; higher US yields are the main risk to the trend.

items.headline: Iran reportedly drops its demand to control Hormuz; Qatar's prime minister takes a revised plan to Washington
items.summary: Iran offers to stop strikes on Gulf-state vessels if funds frozen in Qatar are released; Qatar's plan adds nuclear inspections and an end to the US blockade. No agreement announced; an Iranian official says no talks are under way. Advancing, contested.
items.rationale: A deal reopening Hormuz would cut India's energy and freight costs further; the gap between the sides keeps confidence low.

items.headline: A record 37 ships were attacked in Hormuz in October; India demands unimpeded passage
items.summary: Two more tankers reportedly caught fire after explosions. India flagged risks to its seafarers and pledged support for a detained Indian captain. Attacks persisting despite truce hopes.
items.rationale: Continuing attacks keep freight, insurance and crew costs high and can reverse the oil slide that has lifted Indian markets.

items.headline: Hormuz LNG traffic reaches its highest since the war began; a Gulf producer ships most of it to India
items.summary: Adds to October's surge in Qatari LNG and a new Gulf supply deal last week. Gas supply recovering.
items.rationale: More LNG reaching India eases supply for power, fertiliser and city gas, though prices remain high.

items.headline: EU pledges €60–70 million for Black Sea shipping security as India engages Moscow and Kyiv on food corridors
items.summary: Reports differ on the amount. India's foreign ministry confirms talks with both sides on shipping safety and grain and energy exports. Builds on Monday's mediation offer.
items.rationale: Safer Black Sea shipping would ease world grain and edible oil prices, helping India's food inflation.

items.headline: US wants to sell Venezuelan oil to India to cut reliance on Russian crude
items.summary: Reports question how much India can absorb. Follows record crude imports and a shift from Russian to Gulf grades. New.
items.rationale: Another crude source adds bargaining power on price and lowers sanctions risk, though heavy Venezuelan grades suit only some refineries.
